label: Early copy-phase outputs (recall 1-2) in long sequences
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, never on original tokens or the <DEL> step. Most of its mass (~87%) sits on the first two copy steps after the delimiter (recall_idx 1, i.e. input = orig(0), ~65% of mass; and recall_idx 2, ~22%). Rate climbs steeply with sequence length (L=9 holds 66% of mass, L=8 24%, L<=6 almost nothing). A smaller secondary group fires on the last couple of copy steps of L=9 sequences. Within the recall-1 step the magnitude depends strongly on the token: the largest activations come when orig(0) is b, 3, d, y or q, and recall 1 is usually much stronger than recall 2 in the same sequence. Because of this token dependence, many long-sequence early-copy steps stay below threshold, which keeps precision around 0.6. Adding token-set filters lowered F1, so they were not kept.
